meta.title: Happy Retirement
meta.description: Tax minimization, lifestyle design, and healthcare strategies for a successful retirement.
meta.note: Add a post here once; blogs/happy_retirement.html renders the archive, topic and year filters, and search from this list. 'topics' lists topic ids (first is primary); 'tags' are the pills shown on the card. Leave date null unless the post itself states one.

posts.title: Will Your Retirement Money Last 30 Years?
posts.desc: Understand why retirement may last longer than expected and how inflation and investment growth affect your long-term financial security.
posts.imageAlt: Two hikers with backpacks walking a trail through a tall forest

posts.title: How Much Should You Have Saved by 50?
posts.desc: Understand retirement savings benchmarks, what to do if you are behind, and how to separate near-term spending needs from long-term growth.
posts.imageAlt: A tipped-over glass jar with coins spilling onto a table

posts.title: Where Should Your Next Dollar of Savings Go?
posts.desc: Explore a practical framework for prioritizing emergency savings, employer matches, debt, tax-advantaged accounts, and investments.
posts.imageAlt: Colorful wooden blocks stacked into a small tower, each layer resting on the one below

posts.title: Should You Claim Social Security at 62, 67, or 70?
posts.desc: Explore the trade-offs between claiming early and delaying benefits, including longevity, household income, and spousal considerations.
posts.imageAlt: A typewriter with a sheet of paper reading Social Security

posts.title: What Medicare Doesn't Cover in Retirement
posts.desc: Understand healthcare premiums, out-of-pocket expenses, supplemental coverage, and long-term care planning.
posts.imageAlt: Close-up of a stethoscope on a table

posts.title: Traditional vs. Roth: How to Build a Tax-Smart Retirement Portfolio
posts.desc: Learn how tax-deferred, tax-free, and taxable accounts differ and why managing taxable income can matter in retirement.
posts.imageAlt: A forest path that splits into two roads

posts.title: Which Retirement Account Should You Spend First?
posts.desc: Explore how taxable, traditional retirement, and Roth accounts may fit into a tax-aware withdrawal strategy.
posts.imageAlt: A compass resting on a paper map

posts.title: The Letter That Quietly Cost Over One Million Dollars
posts.desc: It looked like ordinary annual paperwork. It quietly triggered a six-part tax, Medicare, and investment cascade.
posts.imageAlt: Stack of papers representing annual RMD paperwork

posts.title: The Doctor Who Waited Too Long
posts.desc: He spent his career deferring taxes. The expensive mistake was assuming that later would always be better.
posts.imageAlt: Senior doctor seated in a medical office

posts.title: The IRS Was His Silent Business Partner
posts.desc: He spent forty years accumulating $4 million in retirement savings. He thought the whole balance belonged to his family.

posts.title: Bill Left $5.1 Million. Tom Left $3.3 Million. What Happened?
posts.desc: Bill and Tom retired on the same day at 60, each with about $3.8 million saved. A case study in how required minimum distributions and tax timing led to very different results.

posts.title: Roth Conversions: Compressing Tax Liabilities Pre-Medicare
posts.desc: Timing your tax conversions during lower-income gap years keeps your lifetime tax liabilities minimized and guards against structural Medicare surcharges.
posts.imageAlt: Hand holding a phone calculator next to tax paperwork

posts.title: Navigating Early Retirement ACA Premium Tax Subsidies
posts.desc: Learn the mechanical frameworks required to monitor your Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) to secure maximum health insurance savings.

posts.title: The Expat Medicare Trap: Why Retiring Abroad Won't Save You From Uncle Sam's Late Penalty
posts.desc: Moving overseas at 65 doesn't switch off Medicare's enrollment clock. Skipping Part B abroad can mean a lifetime premium penalty if you ever come home.
posts.imageAlt: A gloved clinician giving a patient an injection
